19.34 Kǒngzǐ said:
"Permissible,
simple."
"Simple" means
uncultivated wilderness.
"Uncultivated wilderness" means
lacking the patterns of propriety.
Kǒngzǐ met with Zǐsāng Bózǐ,
and Zǐsāng Bózǐ was without robes and hat.
His disciples said:
"Why does our Master meet with this person?"
He said:
"His substance is beautiful but without refinement,
I wish to persuade him and refine him."
Kǒngzǐ left.
Zǐsāng Bózǐ's disciples were displeased and
said:
"Why did he meet with Kǒngzǐ?"
He said:
"His substance is beautiful, but his embellishments are excessive;
I wish to explain and remove his embellishments."
Therefore, it is said:
"One who cultivates both substance and embellishment is called a gentleman;
one who has substance but no embellishment is called a simple rustic."
Zǐsāng Bózǐ was a simple rustic,
wishing to equate human morality with that of oxen and horses,
therefore Zhònggōng said:
"Too simple."
Above there is no enlightened Son of Heaven,
below there are no worthy regional hegemons,
the world is considered without principle.
Ministers assassinate their rulers,
sons assassinate their fathers;
if one has the power to punish them,
it is permissible to punish them.
During the time of Confucius,
there was no enlightened Son of Heaven above,
therefore it was said, "Yōng can be made to face south."
To face south [is the position of],
the Son of Heaven.
The reason why Yōng was deemed fit to face south [was that],
when Zǐsāng Bózǐ was asked about by Confucius,
Confucius said:
"Acceptable,
but simple."
Zhònggōng said:
"To abide in reverence and practice simplicity in guiding the people,
is that not acceptable?
To be simple in one's heart and practice simplicity,
is that not excessively simple?"
Confucius said:
"Yōng's words are correct."
Zhòng Gōng was versed in the art of transformation,
Confucius was clear on the kingly way,
yet nothing could be added to Zhòng Gōng's words.
19.35 Confucius arrived outside the outer gate of Qí,
encountering an infant carrying a pot,
traveling together,
his gaze was focused,
his heart was upright,
his conduct was proper.
Confucius said to the driver:
"Quickly drive away from him,
quickly drive away from him!
The 《Sháo》 music is being performed."
Confucius arrived there and heard the 《Sháo》,
for three months he did not know the taste of meat.
Therefore, music is not only for one's own enjoyment,
but also for the enjoyment of others;
not only for one's own rectification,
but also for the rectification of others.
How great it is!
Those who engage in this music,
never imagined that music could reach this level.
19．36 Huángdì (黃帝) issued an edict to Líng Lún (伶倫) to create musical scales.
Líng Lún (伶倫), starting from the west of Dàxià (大夏),
went to the north side of Kūnlún (崑崙) Mountain,
and took bamboo from Xiè Gǔ (嶰谷),
selecting those with evenly spaced holes and uniform thickness.
He cut between two sections,
making them nine inches long and blew into them,
using it as the Gōng (宮) note of the Huángzhōng (黃鍾) scale,
called Hánshǎo (含少).
He then created twelve pipes.
At the foot of Kūnlún (崑崙) Mountain,
he listened to the calls of the phoenix,
to distinguish the twelve lǜ (律) pitches.
The male phoenix called six,
and the female phoenix also called six.
Comparing them to the Gōng (宮) note of the Huángzhōng (黃鍾) scale,
they perfectly matched the Gōng (宮) note of the Huángzhōng (黃鍾) scale,
and could all be derived from it,
thus it is the foundation of the lǜ (律) pitches.
Therefore, it is said:
"The Huángzhōng (黃鍾) note is subtle and even, pure and complete without being damaged.
Qí wèi gōng dú zūn, [Its being the gong note is uniquely honored,]
xiàng dà shèng zhī dé, [it symbolizes the virtue of a great sage,]
kěyǐ míng zhì xián zhī gōng, [and can illuminate the achievements of a supremely virtuous person.]
Gù fèng ér jiàn zhī yú zōngmiào, [Therefore, it is revered and offered in ancestral temples,]
yǐ gē yíng gōngdé, [to sing and welcome meritorious deeds,]
shì shì bù wàng. [generation after generation without forgetting.]
Shì gù huángzhōng shēng línzhōng. [Therefore, Huángzhōng generates Línzhōng.]
Línzhōng shēng dàlǚ, [Línzhōng generates Dàlǚ,]
Dàlǚ shēng yízé, [Dàlǚ generates Yízé,]
Yízé shēng tàicù, [Yízé generates Tàicù,]
Tàicù shēng nánlǚ, [Tàicù generates Nánlǚ,]
Nánlǚ shēng jiázhōng, [Nánlǚ generates Jiázhōng,]
Jiázhōng shēng wúshè, [Jiázhōng generates Wúshè,]
Wúshè shēng gūxǐ, [Wúshè generates Gūxǐ,]
Gūxǐ shēng yìngzhōng, [Gūxǐ generates Yìngzhōng,]
Yìngzhōng shēng ruíbīn. [Yìngzhōng generates Ruíbīn.]
Sānfēn suǒ shēng, [That which is produced by dividing into three,]
yì zhī yī fēn yǐshàng shēng, [adding one part of it generates upwards,]
sānfēn suǒ shēng, [that which is produced by dividing into three,]
qù qí yī fēn yǐxià shēng. [subtracting one part of it generates downwards.]
Huángzhōng, Dàlǚ, Tàicù, Jiázhōng, Gūxǐ, Zhōnglǚ, Ruíbīn wèi shàng, [Huángzhōng, Dàlǚ, Tàicù, Jiázhōng, Gūxǐ, Zhōnglǚ, and Ruíbīn are the upper ones,]
Línzhōng, Yízé, Nánlǚ, Wúshè, Yìngzhōng wèi xià. [Línzhōng, Yízé, Nánlǚ, Wúshè, and Yìngzhōng are the lower ones.]
Dà shèng zhì zhì zhī shì, [In the era of great sage's perfect governance,]
tiāndì zhī qì hé yǐ shēng fēng, [the qi of heaven and earth unite to generate wind,]
rì zhì zé rì xíng qí fēng, [on the solstices, the sun travels its wind,]
yǐ shēng shí'èr lǜ. [to generate the twelve lü.]
Gù zhòngdōng rì duǎn zhì, [Therefore, at the winter solstice, the days are shortest,]
zé shēng huángzhōng, [and Huángzhōng is generated,]
In late winter, *dàlǚ* arises;
in early spring, *tàicù* arises;
in mid-spring, *jiázhōng* arises;
in late spring, *gūxǐ* arises;
in early summer, *zhònglǚ* arises;
in midsummer, when the days are at their longest,
then *ruíbīn* arises;
in late summer, *línzhōng* arises;
in early autumn, *yízé* arises;
in mid-autumn, *nánlǚ* arises;
in late autumn, *wúshè* arises;
in early winter, *yìngzhōng* arises.
When the winds of Heaven and Earth are balanced,
the twelve *lǜ* (pitch pipes) arrive.
19.37 The sage made the rattle drum, the drum, the *qiāng*, the *jié*, the ocarina, and the *chí* flute.
These six [instruments]
are sounds of virtuous music.
Then bells, chimes, the *yú*, and the *sè* are used to harmonize them.
Then shields, axes, yak-tail banners, and bamboo flutes are used to accompany them in dance.
This is the means by which sacrifices are offered in the temple of the former kings.
This is the means by which presentations, feasts, toasts, and reciprocal cups of wine are offered.
It is the means by which official ranks of noble and base are ordered, each obtaining their proper place.
This can be used to show later generations the order of respect between elders and juniors.
19.38 The sound of the bell is *kēng*;
*kēng* is used to establish command;
command is used to establish might;
Harshness establishes military prowess.
When a gentleman hears the sound of bells, he thinks of martial ministers.
The sound of stone is that of the chime-stone.
The chime-stone establishes discrimination,
discrimination leads to death.
When a gentleman hears the sound of the chime-stone, he thinks of ministers who die for the frontiers.
The sound of silk is sorrowful,
sorrow establishes integrity,
integrity establishes aspiration.
When a gentleman hears the sound of zithers and lutes, he thinks of ministers of aspiration and righteousness.
The sound of bamboo is profuse,
profusion establishes assemblies,
assemblies gather the masses.
When a gentleman hears the sound of reed organs, panpipes, and flutes, he thinks of ministers who gather and store resources.
The sound of drums and kettledrums is joyful,
joy establishes movement,
movement advances the masses.
When a gentleman hears the sound of drums and kettledrums, he thinks of ministers who are generals and commanders.
When a gentleman listens to music,
it is not merely to listen to its resounding tones,
but also to find something with which to connect.
19.39 Music is
what the sages delight in,
and it can improve the people's hearts.
Its influence on people is profound,
it changes customs and transforms habits,
therefore the former kings emphasized its teachings.
Now, the people have the nature of blood, vital energy, understanding,
but lack constant feelings of sorrow, joy, love, and anger.
Responding to stimulation and influenced by things, they move,
and then their minds take shape.
Therefore, when the sounds of inciting and dispiriting music are made,
the people think of worry;
when music of leisurely progress, ease, elaborate composition, and simplified rhythm is created,
the people are healthy and happy;
when music of rough intensity, abrupt rise, vigorous conclusion, and expansive energy is created,
the people are resolute and strong;
when music of integrity, directness, strength, uprightness, solemnity, and sincerity is created,
the people are respectful and reverent;
when music of generosity, kindness, acquiescence, accomplishment, harmony, and movement is created,
the people are compassionate and loving;
when music of deviation, seclusion, perversion, dissipation, foreign formation, purging, and excessiveness is created,
the people are dissolute and chaotic.
Therefore, the former kings based it on human nature,
measured it against standards,
regulated it with ritual and righteousness,
contained the harmony of vital energy,
guided the practice of the Five Constants,
making it so that yang does not dissipate,
and yin does not become secretive,
the vigor does not become anger,
the gentleness does not become fear,
the four energies flow freely in the middle and manifest outwardly,
all being secure in their positions and not conflicting with each other.
After that, they established schools,
Broaden its rhythms,
reduce its embellishments,
so as to measure the depth of virtue.
Regulate the terms of small and large,
compare the order of beginning and end,
to symbolize the course of affairs,
so that the principles of closeness and distance, nobility and lowliness, age and youth, male and female,
are all visibly manifested in music.
Therefore, it is said:
Music,
observe its depths!
If the soil is exhausted, then grasses and trees will not grow;
if the water is turbulent, then fish and turtles will not become large;
if the vital energy is weak, then living things will not thrive;
if the world is in chaos, then ritual will be perverse and music will be licentious.
Therefore, its sound is mournful but not solemn,
joyful but not peaceful,
careless and easily violating the proper measures,
flowing and unrestrained, forgetting the root.
Broadness allows for wickedness,
narrowness leads to desires,
being affected by the washing away of vitality, and extinguishing the virtue of peace and harmony,
therefore, the gentleman despises it.
Whenever corrupt sounds affect people, perverse vital energy responds to them;
perverse vital energy forms images, and licentious music arises.
Correct sounds affect people, and harmonious vital energy responds to them;
harmonious vital energy forms images, and harmonious music arises.
Singing and responding have their echoes;
Returning the crooked and straightening the bent, each goes to its allotted share,
and the principles of all things
move each other according to their kind.
Therefore, the gentleman reverses emotions to harmonize his will,
and compares categories to accomplish his actions.
Treacherous sounds and disordered colors are not practiced in listening,
licentious pleasure and perverse rites are not connected to the mind,
the spirits of sloth, negligence, evil, and perversity are not established in the body,
causing ears, eyes, nose, mouth, heart, intelligence, and the hundred limbs all to follow and obey correctness, thus enacting their proper meaning.
Then, it is emitted as sound,
patterned with zithers and lutes,
moved with shields and axes,
adorned with feathers and yak tails,
accompanied by panpipes and flutes,
displaying the light of utmost virtue,
moving the harmony of the four seasons,
to reveal the principles of all things.
Therefore, its purity and brightness resemble heaven,
its breadth and greatness resemble earth,
its beginning and end resemble the four seasons,
its revolutions resemble wind and rain;
the five colors form patterns without disorder,
the eight winds follow the pitch-standards without treachery,
the hundred measures obtain their numbers and have constancy;
small and large complement each other,
beginning and end produce each other,
singing and harmony, clear and turbid,
alternately serve as warp threads.
Therefore, when music is practiced, ethical relationships become clear,
ears and eyes become sharp and perceptive,
blood and qi become harmonious and balanced,
customs are transformed and habits are changed,
and the world becomes peaceful.
Therefore, it is said:
Music
is joy.
The junzi (jūnzǐ) finds joy in attaining the Dao (Dào),
the xiaoren (xiǎorén) finds joy in attaining their desires.
Using the Dao (Dào) to control desires
results in joy without disorder.
Using desires to forget the Dao (Dào)
results in confusion and no joy.
Therefore, the junzi (jūnzǐ) reflects on their feelings to harmonize their intentions,
and broadens music to complete their teachings.
Therefore, when music is practiced, the people are guided in the right direction,
and one can observe virtue.
Virtue
is the beginning of one's nature;
music
is the flowering of virtue;
metal, stone, silk, and bamboo
are the instruments of music.
Poetry speaks of one's aspirations;
singing expresses its sound;
dance expresses its form.
These three originate from the heart,
Then the spirit of music follows it.
Therefore, when feelings are deep, they become refined;
when the vital force is strong, it transforms into spirit;
harmony and smoothness accumulate within, and outstanding qualities radiate outward;
only music cannot be feigned.
Music,
is the movement of the heart;
sound,
is the image of music;
ornate patterns and rhythms,
are the embellishments of sound.
The superior man moves its root,
enjoys its image,
and then regulates its embellishments.
Therefore, first drums are used for warning,
three steps are taken to reveal direction,
a restart is used to mark the past,
disorder is repeated to embellish the return,
striving quickly without becoming insolent,
extremely subtle without being hidden.
Enjoying his will alone,
without being satiated with his way;
comprehensively performing his way,
without selfishly indulging his desires.
Therefore, feelings are revealed and righteousness is established,
when music ends, virtue is honored.
The superior man uses it to love goodness,
the petty man uses embellishments to listen to his faults.
Therefore, it is said:
In the way of governing the people,
music is of utmost importance.
19.40 Among musical instruments suitable for intimate enjoyment,
the qín (zither) is the most fitting.
The gentleman cultivates virtue through it,
hence he keeps it close.
All sounds originate
from the human heart.
The movements of the human heart
are caused by external things.
Being moved by external things causes action,
hence sound is formed;
sounds resonate with each other,
thus changes arise;
when these changes are patterned, they are called music (yīn);
organizing the sounds and enjoying them,
along with shields, axes, feathers, and yak tails, is called music (lè).
Music (lè)
is that which arises from sound (yīn),
its root lies in the heart's response to external things.
Therefore, when the heart is moved by sorrow,
its sound is jiào and sharp;
when the heart is moved by joy,
its sound is chǎn and slow;
when the heart is moved by delight,
its sound is fā and scattered;
Qí nù xīn gǎn zhě,
their voices are forceful and severe;
those whose hearts are moved by respect,
their voices are upright and principled;
those whose hearts are moved by love,
their voices are harmonious and balanced.
The goodness or badness of people
is not (due to) their nature,
(but) they are moved by things and then act;
therefore, the former kings were careful about that by which people are moved.
Therefore, ritual (lǐ) is used to determine their intentions,
music (yuè) is used to harmonize their nature,
governance (zhèng) is used to unify their actions,
punishment (xíng) is used to prevent their treachery.
Ritual, music, punishment, and governance,
their ultimate goal is the same,
that is, to unify the people's hearts and establish the way of governance.
19.41 All sounds arise from the human heart.
Emotions move within and take shape in sound,
sound that forms patterns is called music (yīn).
Therefore, the music of a well-governed age is peaceful and joyful,
its governance is harmonious;
the music of a chaotic age is resentful and angry,
its governance is perverse;
the music of a collapsing state is sorrowful and longing,
its people are distressed.
The principles of music
are connected with governance.
The *gōng* note represents the ruler,
the *shāng* note represents the ministers,
the *jué* note represents the people,
the *zhǐ* note represents affairs,
the *yǔ* note represents things.
If the five notes are disordered, then there is no law.
The sounds of lawlessness:
if the *gōng* note is disordered, then there is ruin,
and the ruler is arrogant;
if the *shāng* note is disordered, then there is collapse,
and the officials are corrupt;
if the *jiǎo* note is disordered, then there is worry,
and the people are resentful;
if the *zhǐ* note is disordered, then there is sorrow,
and the affairs are toilsome;
if the *yǔ* note is disordered, then there is danger,
and the wealth is depleted.
If all five are disordered,
and each replaces the other, it is called insolence.
If it is like this,
then the destruction of the state will be imminent.
The music of Zhèng and Wèi,
is the music of a disordered era,
comparable to insolence.
The music of Sāngjiān and Púshàng,
is the music of a ruined state,
its government is scattered,
The people are scattered,
falsely accusing superiors and acting selfishly, and this cannot be stopped.
19.42 Generally, those who have misfortune and calamity
arise from excessive indulgence and arrogance.
The root of excessive indulgence and arrogance
arises from drinking alcohol.
Therefore, the ancients were careful about the rites of drinking alcohol,
making the ears listen to refined music,
the eyes observe correct etiquette,
the feet perform correct deportment,
the heart discuss correct principles,
therefore, drinking alcohol all day without fault.
For those who are near, several days,
for those who are far, several months,
all people have virtue in them to increase goodness.
The "Book of Odes" says:
"Having become drunk with wine,
having become satisfied with virtue."
This is what it means.
19.43 Generally, of things that enter from the outside,
none is deeper than sound,
which changes people most extremely.
Therefore, the sages accordingly perfect it with virtue, calling it music.
Music
is the wind of virtue.
The "Book of Odes" says:
"Dignified deportment is subdued,
virtuous sounds are orderly."
This refers to rites and music.
Therefore, the noble man uses rites to rectify the outside,
and uses music to rectify the inside.
If the inside is even momentarily separated from music,
then perverse influences arise.
If externally one momentarily departs from ritual,
then lax conduct begins.
Therefore, in ancient times, the Son of Heaven and the feudal lords listened to the sound of bells,
and never departed from the courtyard.
High officials and grand officers listened to the qín (zither) and sè (lute),
and never departed from before them.
This was how they cultivated a correct mind and extinguished licentious influences.
Music, when it stirs internally,
causes people to easily follow the Dao and love goodness.
Music, when it stirs externally,
causes people to be warm, respectful, and refined.
The sounds of the Ya and Song stir people and are responded to with upright qi (vital energy).
The sounds of harmony, accomplishment, beauty, and goodness stir people and are responded to with harmonious qi.
The sounds of rough, fierce, violent, and rushing stir people and are responded to with angry qi.
The sounds of Zheng and Wei stir people and are responded to with licentious qi.
Therefore, the junzi is careful about what he uses to stir people.
19.44 Zǐ Lù played the sè (zither) with sounds of the northern borders.
Confucius heard it and said,
"Indeed,
Yóu is not talented."
Rǎn Yǒu was in attendance,
and Confucius said:
"Qiú, come here.
Why don't you tell Yóu about this?
The ancient kings, in creating music,
played central notes,
formed moderate rhythms,
flowed towards the south,
and did not return to the north.
The south is the region of birth and growth,
while the north is the territory of killing and war.
Therefore, the gentleman holds the center as the foundation,
and strives for life as the basis.
Thus, his music is warm and harmonious, and dwells in the center,
to symbolize the Qi of birth and growth.
Feelings of sorrow, grief, and pain
do not reach his heart;
movements of violence, excess, and wildness
do not reside in his body.
Those who are like this possess the wind of governance and preservation,
and the practice of peace and joy.
Petty men, however, are not like this;
they grasp the branch to discuss the root,
and strive for rigidity as the basis.
Thus, their music is cold and harsh, and petty and trivial,
to symbolize the Qi of killing and war.
Feelings of harmony, rhythm, and uprightness
do not reach their hearts;
Wēn Yǎn’s 溫儼 movements of respect and solemnity,
did not reside in his bearing.
For, killing
is the wind of chaos and ruin,
the deed of fleeing in defeat.
Formerly, Shùn 舜 created the music of the Southern Wind;
its rise was vigorous,
and to this day, kings and dukes follow it and do not abandon it.
Zhòu 紂 created the music of the Northern Border;
its decline was sudden,
and to this day, kings and dukes take it as a laughingstock.
Shùn 舜, as a commoner,
accumulated righteousness and embraced benevolence,
practiced moderation and performed good deeds, and ultimately rose to prominence.
Zhòu 紂, as the Son of Heaven,
indulged in arrogance, licentiousness, and dissipation,
and was obstinate, violent, and cruel, and ultimately perished.
Now, Yóu 由 is merely a follower,
a humble commoner.
He has no regard for the institutions of the former kings,
and further, he possesses the music of a fallen kingdom.
How can he possibly protect his seven-foot body?"
Rǎn Yǒu 冉有 told Zǐlù 子路 about this.
Zǐlù 子路 said:
"It is Yóu’s 由 fault.
As a petty man, I am incapable of understanding.
I have fallen and become mired in this.
It is fitting that the Master speaks thus!"
Consequently, he repented,
and did not eat.
After seven days, he was reduced to skin and bones.
Kǒngzǐ 孔子 said:
"Yóu’s 由 repentance
is excessive."
Returning to Simplicity
20.1 Kǒngzǐ performed divination,
and the hexagram he obtained was "Bì" (Adornment).
He sighed deeply and looked up to the sky,
feeling uneasy.
Zǐ Zhāng stepped forward
and, raising his hand, asked:
"Did the Master hear that 'Bì' is an auspicious hexagram, yet still sigh over it?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"'Bì' is not the true color,
and that is why I sigh about it.
I think of the natural state,
the purity.
White should be truly white,
black should be truly black.
What is the natural state?
I have also heard that
red lacquer does not need patterns,
white jade does not need carving,
precious pearls do not need adornment.
Why is this?
Hé yě?
Those who possess excess substance
do not accept adornment."
20.2 Those who trust in ghosts and spirits lose their plans,
and those who trust in lucky days lose their timing.
How can we know this is true?
The wise sages thoroughly understand
and are able to achieve success without relying on specific days;
they respect laws and decrees,
value merit and labor,
and experience good fortune without divination;
they carefully practice benevolence and righteousness,
follow principles of reason,
and receive blessings without prayer and sacrifice.
Therefore, choosing days through divination and numerology,
purification through fasting and abstinence,
fattening sacrificial animals,
adorning jade and precious stones,
performing elaborate sacrifices,
ultimately cannot remove the disasters of rebellion and wickedness.
To serve the spirits as if they were intelligent
while intending to act wrongly and rebelliously,
and then seek blessings through sacrifices,
the spirits will certainly oppose it.
The Son of Heaven sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the Five Peaks, and the Four Rivers;
the feudal lords sacrifice to the gods of soil and grain;
the high officials sacrifice to the Five Household Gods;
Scholars sacrifice to the gate and household,
commoners sacrifice to their ancestors.
Sage-kings received Heaven's will,
and instituted rites accordingly.
All those in ancient times who divined the day
did so to assist in the Way and resolve doubts,
showing there was something prior and they dared not act on their own authority,
not wishing to use wickedness to overturn things and luckily secure complete safety.
Confucius said:
"To sacrifice to spirits that are not one's own is
flattery."
Therefore, Mount Tài never enjoyed the sacrifices of the Jìshì clan.
The *Book of Changes* says, "The east neighbor slaughtering an ox
is not as good as the west neighbor's spring sacrifice,"
for it values rites, not things;
it reveres substance, not ostentation.
If one truly possesses virtue and extends it,
then where can one not go?
Therefore, when sages see a person's outward appearance,
they must examine his inner quality.
20.3 Those who farmed in Lìshān were good at encroaching on boundaries,
and Shùn plowed there;
those who fished in Léizé were good at fighting over dikes,
and Shùn fished there;
the pottery of the eastern 夷 was inferior,
and Shùn made pottery there.
Therefore, plowing, fishing, and pottery were not Shùn's business,
And Shùn did this
in order to rescue the situation from failure.
The nature of the people is that they cannot overcome their desires;
they abandon the substance and return to the superficial.
Therefore, things become inferior and inadequate,
and the calamity of strife and contention arises.
The calamity of strife and contention arises,
and thus comes the tendency to steal.
The reason for this
is what?
It is due to departing from sincerity and embracing deception,
abandoning simplicity and adopting falsehood.
They pursue the trivial ends without any rest.
If the sage suppresses their ornamentation and elevates their substance,
then the world will turn around.
20.4 The *Book of Poetry* says:
"The cuckoo is in the mulberry tree,
it has seven young ones.
The virtuous and good person,
their deportment is unified."
The *Commentary* says:
The reason why the cuckoo can raise seven chicks
is that it has a single mind.
The reason why the gentleman can govern all things
is that he has a single standard.
To govern things with a single standard
is the mind of Heaven.
The five do not separate,
and combine to become one,
this is called the "Mind of Heaven."
With me, I can deeply concentrate my intention on one,
therefore, with one heart, one can serve a hundred lords,
but with a hundred hearts, one cannot serve even one lord,
thus sincerity is not far away.
Now, sincerity
is oneness,
oneness
is substance.
Although a gentleman may have external adornments,
he will certainly not depart from his inner substance.
20.5 In Wèi there were five men,
all carrying jars to enter a well,
to water chives,
finishing only one patch in a day.
Dèng Xī passed by,
got out of his carriage and taught them, saying:
"Make a machine,
weighting its rear,
and lightening its front,
call it a "sweep" (a well sweep),
irrigating chives all day,
and you will not tire even after a hundred patches."
The five men said:
"Our teacher said:
'Where there is cleverness in contrivance,
there must be failure in contrivance.'
It's not that I don't know this,
but I don't want to do it.
You may leave,
I am single-mindedly irrigating,
I don't know how to change."
Dèng Xī left,
traveling dozens of *lǐ*,
his expression was unhappy,
he fell ill.
His disciple said:
"Who is this person who resents our lord?
Please allow me to kill him for the lord."
Dèng Xī said:
"Release him,
he is what is called a true man,
he can be made to guard the state."
20.6 Qín Huá Lí asked Mòzǐ,
"Brocade and embroidered linen,
what use are they?"
Mòzǐ said:
"Alas!
These are not things I concern myself with.
In ancient times, there were those without such embellishments who succeeded,
Xià Yǔ was one of them,
living in humble and small palaces,
Reducing food and drink,
earth steps of three levels,
clothing of coarse cloth.
At this time,
embroidered ceremonial robes were of no use, and the focus was on completeness and sturdiness.
Pángēng of the Yin [dynasty],
enlarged the houses of his former kings,
and moved the capital to Yin,
not cutting the thatched roofs,
not hewing the painted rafters,
in order to change the view of the world.
At this time,
where could colorful silks
be used?
The common people are not self-motivated,
they take the ruler as their model.
If the ruler above does not do it,
how would the people below use them?
These two kings took the lead in the world,
therefore their influence flourished in their time,
and their fame was established in the present age.
Moreover, brocades and fine hemp cloth
are what rulers of chaotic states create,
and their origins all arose in Qi.
Duke Jǐng of Qi loved extravagance and forgot frugality,
fortunately he had Yànzǐ to admonish him with frugality,
but even then he almost could not overcome [extravagance].
Alas, how can extravagance be exhausted?
Zhòu constructed the Deer Terrace and mounds of distiller's grains,
wine ponds and meat forests,
palace walls adorned with paintings,
carvings and engravings,
brocade and embroidery covering the halls,
gold, jade, and precious ornaments,
women singing and acting,
bells, drums, pipes, and strings,
flowing unrestrained,
and the world became increasingly exhausted.
Therefore, in the end, he died and the state perished,
was executed by all under Heaven,
was it not only because of the use of brocade and coarse cloth!
Now, in a year of famine,
someone wants to give you a pearl of the Marquis of Suí,
saying:
"It cannot be sold,
a treasure to be used as adornment."
Someone else wants to give you a *zhong* of grain;
the one who gets the pearl cannot get the grain,
the one who gets the grain cannot get the pearl,
what will you choose?"
Qín Huálí said:
"I will take the grain,
it can save the poor."
Mòzǐ said:
"Indeed,
then what is the harm in serving extravagance?
Length that is useless,
fondness for trivial extravagance,

but did not hit him.
He hit the tassels (of the crown),
destroying them.
Marquis Wén turned to his attendants and said,
"For a subject to strike his lord,
what is the punishment?"
The attendants said,
"The punishment should be boiling."
He dragged Shī Jīng down one step from the hall.
Shī Jīng said,
"May your subject be allowed to speak one word before I die?"
Marquis Wén said,
"You may."
*Shī Jīng* says:
"In the past, when Yáo and Shùn were rulers,
they only feared that their words would not be opposed by the people.
When Jié and Zhòu were rulers,
they only feared that their words would be opposed by the people.
The minister who struck Jié and Zhòu
was not striking my ruler."
Wén Hóu said:
"Release him;
this is my fault.
Hang a zither at the city gate
to remind me;
do not mend the tassels of my crown
to warn me."
1.39 Qí Jǐng Gōng was enjoying himself at Lóu,
when he heard of the death of Yàn Zǐ.
The Duke, dressed in plain clothes, rode in a post carriage and drove swiftly.
Thinking himself too slow,
he got out of the carriage and ran.
Realizing he was not as fast as the carriage,
he got back in.
By the time he reached the capital,
he had gotten out of the carriage and ran four times,
weeping as he went.
Upon arrival,
he prostrated himself before the corpse and wailed, saying:
"You, Master, reproached me day and night,
Not leaving out even an inch,
I, your unworthy servant, still indulged in excessive pleasures and did not restrain myself,
causing resentment and offenses to accumulate heavily upon the people.
Now Heaven sends misfortune upon the state of Qí,
not upon me, your unworthy servant, but upon you, Master (Yàn Zǐ),

1.40 Seventeen years after Yàn Zǐ's death,
Duke Jǐng was drinking with his high officials,
the Duke shot and missed the target,
those in the hall all cried "Excellent!",

The Duke changed countenance, sighed deeply,
and put down his bow and arrows.
Xián Zhāng entered.
The Duke said,
"Zhāng!
Since I lost Yàn Zǐ seventeen years ago,
I have never heard of my faults.
Now I shoot and miss the target,
and those who cry 'Excellent!' do so as if from a single mouth."
Xián Zhāng replied,
"This is due to the unworthiness of these officials.
Their knowledge is insufficient to perceive your faults,
their courage is insufficient to offend your countenance,
however, there is one thing
your servant has heard:
“If the ruler is fond of it,
then the subjects will submit to it;
if the ruler is addicted to it,

The inchworm, when it eats yellow, its body becomes yellow;

The Duke said,

Today’s words,

At that time, the fishermen brought in fish,

Xián Zhāng returned,

and he stroked the hand of his driver, saying,
"Those who previously sang praises
all desired to be like these fish.
In the past, Yàn Zǐ refused rewards in order to correct the ruler,
therefore mistakes and faults were not covered up.
Now the ministers flatter and fawn to seek profit,
so they offer their integrity and sing praises,
as if from a single mouth.
Now, my assistance to the ruler has not yet been seen by the public,
and I receive this fish,
this is to go against the righteousness of Yàn Zǐ and to follow the desires of flattery."
He firmly declined the fish and did not accept it.
The noble man said,
"The incorruptibility of Xián Zhāng
is indeed a legacy of Yàn Zǐ's conduct."

1.44 Those who respect the ruler and demean the ministers,

If power is lost, authority will falter.
Therefore, if the Son of Heaven loses the Way,
then the feudal lords will be honored;
if the feudal lords lose governance,
then the grand officers will rise;
if the grand officers lose their offices,
then the common people will rise up.
From this, it can be seen that
it has never happened that the superiors lose and the inferiors gain.
1.45 Confucius said:

if the Virtue of Shang had not declined,
the Virtue of Zhou would not have arisen;
if the Virtue of Zhou had not declined,
the *Spring and Autumn Annals* would not have been written.
Only after the *Spring and Autumn Annals* were written did gentlemen know that the Way of Zhou had declined."
Therefore, the relationship between superiors and inferiors is one of mutual undermining,
like water and fire destroying each other.
A ruler must not fail to observe and greatly empower his ministers,
for this is when private houses flourish and the public family is ruined.
If a ruler does not observe this,
then the state will be in danger.
Guǎnzi said:
"Authority should not be divided;
government should not have two gates."
Therefore, it is said:
"If the shin is bigger than the thigh, it is difficult to walk;
if the finger is bigger than the arm, it is difficult to grasp."
If the root is small and the branch is large,
they cannot control each other.
